js-basics.title: Values, variables and types
js-basics.summary: Start here if you are new. A program stores values in named boxes and combines them. This station covers the boxes (variables), what can go in them (types) and how to combine them (operators).

headings.text: Step 1: a variable is a named box
Step 2: types, the kinds of values
Step 6: turning one type into another

js-basics.videoTitle: JavaScript Data Types and Variables Easily Explained, by DevStart (8 min)

js-functions-flow.title: Functions, conditions and loops
js-functions-flow.summary: A program makes decisions, repeats work and packages steps so they can be reused. Conditions, loops and functions are the three tools, and functions are the one the rest of JavaScript is built around.

headings.text: Step 4: scope, where a name can be seen

js-functions-flow.videoTitle: Learn JavaScript Arrow Functions in 8 minutes, by Bro Code

js-objects-arrays.title: Objects, arrays and destructuring
js-objects-arrays.summary: Real data comes in groups. An object groups values by name, an array groups them by position. Reading, changing, looping over and unpacking these two shapes is most of everyday JavaScript.

headings.text: Step 3: destructuring, unpacking in one line

js-objects-arrays.videoTitle: JavaScript Destructuring in 8 minutes, by Bro Code

js-execution-context.title: Execution context and hoisting
js-execution-context.summary: Before one line of your code runs, the engine has already made a pass over it. That pass explains hoisting, the temporal dead zone and the call stack.
js-execution-context.videoTitle: JavaScript Visualized: Execution Contexts, by Lydia Hallie (12 min)

js-closures.title: Scope and closures
js-closures.summary: A function remembers the variables around the place it was written, even after that place has finished running. Private state, React hooks, debounce and middleware factories all rest on this.
js-closures.videoTitle: JavaScript Visualized: Closures, by Lydia Hallie (12 min)

js-this.title: this, call, apply, bind
js-this.summary: The value of this is not decided where a function is written. It is decided at the moment the function is called. Four rules cover every case.
js-this.videoTitle: JavaScript this Keyword, by Programming with Mosh (8 min)
js-this.videoSearch: JavaScript this keyword call apply bind explained

js-prototypes.title: Prototypes and classes
js-prototypes.summary: JavaScript objects inherit by linking to other objects. Classes are a cleaner syntax over that same link.
js-prototypes.videoTitle: JavaScript Prototypes Explained Visually, by Outside The Normal (3 min)

js-values.title: Values, references, equality
js-values.summary: Primitives are copied, objects are shared by reference. That one distinction explains equality surprises, accidental mutation and why React asks you to never mutate state.
js-values.videoTitle: Reference Vs Value In JavaScript, by Web Dev Simplified (15 min)
js-values.videoSearch: JavaScript value vs reference shallow copy deep copy explained

js-functional.title: Higher-order functions, debounce, throttle
js-functional.summary: Functions that take or return functions. Once closures click, map/filter/reduce, debounce, throttle and currying are small variations of one idea, and all four are standard interview coding questions.
js-functional.videoTitle: Learn Debounce And Throttle In 16 Minutes, by Web Dev Simplified
js-functional.videoSearch: debounce vs throttle JavaScript explained animation

js-event-loop.title: The event loop
js-event-loop.summary: JavaScript runs one thing at a time, yet handles timers, network calls and clicks without freezing. The event loop is the scheduler that makes this work, and its ordering rules are asked in almost every interview.
js-event-loop.videoTitle: JavaScript Visualized: Event Loop, Web APIs, (Micro)task Queue, by Lydia Hallie (13 min)

js-promises.title: Promises and async/await
js-promises.summary: A promise is an object that stands for a result you do not have yet. Chaining, error handling and running work in parallel all follow from three states and one scheduling rule.
js-promises.videoTitle: JavaScript Visualized: Promise Execution, by Lydia Hallie (9 min)

js-errors.title: Errors and defensive code
js-errors.summary: Things fail. Networks drop, input is wrong, files are missing. Error handling is how a program notices a failure, stops the damage and tells the right person, in synchronous and asynchronous code.

headings.text: Step 2: the Error object and built-in types
Step 5: patterns that keep code healthy

js-errors.videoTitle: try, catch, finally, throw: error handling in JavaScript, by freeCodeCamp (6 min)

js-modules.title: Modules: CommonJS and ES modules
js-modules.summary: A real program is hundreds of files. Modules let each file keep its own names private and share only what it chooses. JavaScript has two module systems, and knowing how they differ explains a whole class of confusing errors.
js-modules.videoTitle: Import vs Require: The Biggest JavaScript Divide, by Matt Pocock (4 min)
js-modules.videoSearch: Modules: CommonJS and ES modules explained

js-iterators.title: Iterators, generators and async iteration
js-iterators.summary: for...of, spread and destructuring all work through one small protocol. Generators are functions that can pause, which makes that protocol easy to implement and lets you produce values one at a time, even an endless number of them.
js-iterators.videoTitle: Learn JavaScript Generators In 12 Minutes, by Web Dev Simplified
js-iterators.videoSearch: Iterators, generators and async iteration explained

js-memory.title: Memory, garbage collection and leaks
js-memory.summary: JavaScript frees memory for you, but only memory that nothing can reach any more. A leak is memory you are still holding by accident. Knowing how the collector decides explains every leak pattern and what WeakMap is for.
js-memory.videoTitle: JavaScript Memory Management Explained: How Garbage Collection Works, by Coding 4 Dev (6 min)
js-memory.videoSearch: Memory, garbage collection and leaks explained

js-build-it.title: Build it yourself: Promise, EventEmitter, bind
js-build-it.summary: The final test of the JavaScript line. Rebuild the tools you have been using, call, apply and bind, an event emitter and a working Promise, from nothing. If you can write these, you understand this, closures, the event loop and promises for real.
js-build-it.videoTitle: JavaScript Interview Question: Implement a Promise Polyfill, by Js For Interview (10 min)
js-build-it.videoSearch: Build it yourself: Promise, EventEmitter, bind explained

node-http-basics.title: How the web talks: clients, servers, HTTP
node-http-basics.summary: Before any framework, understand the conversation. A client sends a request, a server sends back a response, and both are plain text with a fixed shape. This station builds a server with nothing but Node so you can see every part.

headings.text: Step 1: what a request and a response look like
Step 4: a real server with only Node
What happens before the request: the journey

node-http-basics.videoTitle: The HTTP and the Web: the Request-Response Cycle, by The TechCave (9 min)
node-http-basics.videoSearch: How the web talks: clients, servers, HTTP explained

node-essentials.title: Node essentials: files, paths, environment, npm
node-essentials.summary: Node lets JavaScript leave the browser. It can read files, start servers and run programs. This station covers the everyday toolkit, files and paths, configuration through the environment, and npm.
node-essentials.videoTitle: Node.js Ultimate Beginner's Guide in 7 Easy Steps, by Fireship (16 min)
node-essentials.videoSearch: Node essentials: files, paths, environment, npm explained

express-first-app.title: Your first Express API
express-first-app.summary: Express removes the chores from a raw Node server. This station builds a complete small API step by step. Routes, reading input, sending responses, and splitting the code into files.

headings.text: Step 1: the request object, three places input arrives
Step 4: split it into files with a Router

express-first-app.videoTitle: RESTful APIs in 100 Seconds: Build an API from Scratch with Node.js Express, by Fireship (11 min)

node-runtime.title: How Node runs your code
node-runtime.summary: Node is V8 plus libuv. One thread runs your JavaScript, the operating system and a small thread pool do the waiting. Knowing which work goes where tells you what Node is good at and what will freeze it.
node-runtime.videoTitle: Node.js Event Loop Explained in 3D: Call Stack, Microtasks, Libuv, by Code in Motion (12 min)
node-runtime.videoSearch: Node.js event loop libuv phases explained animation

express-middleware.title: Express and the middleware chain
express-middleware.summary: An Express app is a list of functions that a request passes through in order. Routing, body parsing, authentication and error handling are all the same mechanism.
express-middleware.videoTitle: Learn Express Middleware In 14 Minutes, by Web Dev Simplified

rest-api.title: REST API design
rest-api.summary: REST is a set of conventions that make an HTTP API predictable. Resources are nouns, methods are verbs, status codes report the outcome, and idempotency keeps retries safe.
rest-api.videoTitle: What Is REST API? Examples And How To Use It, by ByteByteGo (5 min)
rest-api.videoSearch: REST API design best practices status codes idempotency

node-validation-security.title: Validation and API security
node-validation-security.summary: Everything a client sends is under the client's control. This station covers checking input before using it, and the attacks that work when you do not. Injection, XSS, CSRF, CORS mistakes and mass assignment, each shown working and then fixed.
node-validation-security.videoTitle: API Security Explained: Rate Limiting, CORS, SQL Injection, CSRF, XSS and More, by Hayk Simonyan (9 min)

auth-jwt.title: Authentication: hashing, sessions, JWT
auth-jwt.summary: Proving who a user is, remembering it across requests, and deciding what they may do. Password hashing, sessions vs tokens, the JWT format and where it breaks.

headings.text: Part 2: staying logged in, sessions vs tokens
Part 4: the full flow in Express

auth-jwt.videoTitle: Session vs Token Authentication in 100 Seconds, by Fireship

node-testing.title: Testing a Node API
node-testing.summary: A test is code that runs your code and checks the result, so a change that breaks something is caught in seconds instead of by a user. This station covers unit and integration tests, test doubles and how to write code that is easy to test.

headings.text: Step 1: a test is just an assertion
Step 3: what to test, the edges
Step 5: an integration test of an API
Step 6: test doubles, replacing what you do not control
Step 7: test-driven development in one cycle

node-testing.videoTitle: Integration Testing in Node.js with Jest and Supertest, by Coding 4 Dev (6 min)

websockets.title: WebSockets and real-time
websockets.summary: HTTP only speaks when the client asks. A WebSocket is one long-lived connection where either side can send at any time, which is what chat, live cursors and collaborative editing need.
websockets.videoTitle: WebSockets in 100 Seconds and Beyond with Socket.io, by Fireship (9 min)

node-scaling.title: Scaling Node: queues, caching, rate limits
node-scaling.summary: What to do when one Node process is not enough. Use every core, move slow work to a queue, cache what is read often and limit what any one client can ask for.

headings.text: Tool 2: background jobs with a queue

node-scaling.videoTitle: Rate Limiter System Design: Token Bucket, Leaky Bucket, Scaling, by ByteByteGo (8 min)
node-scaling.videoSearch: system design caching rate limiting message queue animation ByteByteGo

node-production.title: Running in production: config, logging, Docker, deploys
node-production.summary: Code that works on your laptop is half the job. This station covers what turns it into a service others can rely on. Logging, health checks, graceful shutdown, containers, and an automated path from a push to a running deployment.

headings.text: Step 6: CI/CD, from push to production

node-production.videoTitle: Learn Docker in 7 Easy Steps, by Fireship (11 min)
node-production.videoSearch: Running in production: config, logging, Docker, deploys explained

mongo-modeling.title: Documents and data modeling
mongo-modeling.summary: MongoDB stores JSON-like documents. The central design decision is whether related data lives inside one document or in separate documents linked by id, and the answer comes from how the app reads it.
mongo-modeling.videoTitle: 11 Guidelines for Embedding or Referencing in MongoDB, by MongoDB (6 min)
mongo-modeling.videoSearch: MongoDB schema design embedding vs referencing explained

mongo-indexes.title: Indexes and query plans
mongo-indexes.summary: Without an index the database reads every document to answer a query. An index is a sorted structure that lets it jump straight to the matches, at the cost of slower writes.
mongo-indexes.videoTitle: MongoDB Compound Indexes: Workload Analysis and Index Field Order, by MongoDB (14 min)
mongo-indexes.videoSearch: MongoDB indexes compound index ESR rule explain

mongo-aggregation.title: The aggregation pipeline
mongo-aggregation.summary: find returns documents as they are stored. The aggregation pipeline reshapes them: filter, group, join and compute in a sequence of stages, each feeding the next.
mongo-aggregation.videoTitle: Master MongoDB Aggregation Pipeline: $match, $unwind, $group, $project, by MongoDB (5 min)

mongo-transactions.title: Transactions, replication, sharding
mongo-transactions.summary: What MongoDB guarantees when several documents must change together, when a server dies, and when the data no longer fits on one machine.
mongo-transactions.videoTitle: MongoDB Architecture for Beginners: Data Hierarchy, Replication and Sharding, by MongoDB (6 min)
mongo-transactions.videoSearch: MongoDB replica set sharding explained animation

react-rendering.title: Rendering, reconciliation, keys
react-rendering.summary: In React you describe what the screen should look like for the current data. React works out the smallest set of DOM changes. Rendering, reconciliation and keys explain when and why that happens.
react-rendering.videoTitle: The Magic of React's Reconciliation, by Code Sketched (5 min)
react-rendering.videoSearch: React rendering reconciliation virtual DOM keys explained

react-state.title: State, props and hooks
react-state.summary: Props flow down, state lives inside, and every render sees its own frozen copy of both. That snapshot idea explains batching, stale values and why state must never be mutated.

headings.text: The rules of hooks, and why they exist

react-state.videoTitle: Why React setState Doesn't Update Immediately: State Snapshots and Batching, by Runtime Visuals (4 min)

react-effects.title: Effects and the component lifecycle
react-effects.summary: Rendering must be pure, yet apps need to fetch data, open sockets and start timers. useEffect is where a component synchronizes with the world outside React, and its dependency array and cleanup are where most bugs live.
react-effects.videoTitle: Learn useEffect In 13 Minutes, by Web Dev Simplified
react-effects.videoSearch: React useEffect dependency array cleanup explained

react-performance.title: Performance and memoization
react-performance.summary: React is fast by default. When it is not, the cause is almost always too many renders, renders that are too expensive, or too much JavaScript shipped. Each has a specific tool.
react-performance.videoTitle: React.memo vs useCallback vs useMemo Explained with Examples, by Gajanan Tech Hub (13 min)
react-performance.videoSearch: React memo useMemo useCallback explained when to use

react-app-state.title: App state, data fetching, routing
react-app-state.summary: Once an app has many screens, the questions change. Where does shared state live, how is server data cached and kept fresh, and how do URLs map to screens and protect private ones?

headings.text: Intuition: four kinds of state, four homes

react-app-state.videoTitle: React Query in 100 Seconds, by Fireship
react-app-state.videoSearch: React Context vs Redux vs React Query explained

hld-framework.title: A framework for any design question
hld-framework.summary: A system design interview is an open question with no single answer. What is graded is the order you think in. This station gives you that order and the arithmetic that makes your choices defensible.
hld-framework.videoTitle: System Design Interview: A Step-By-Step Guide, by ByteByteGo (10 min)
hld-framework.videoSearch: system design interview framework step by step

hld-scaling.title: Load balancing and horizontal scaling
hld-scaling.summary: One server is a ceiling and a single point of failure. Scaling out means many identical servers behind a load balancer, and that only works if the servers hold no state of their own.
hld-scaling.videoTitle: How Load Balancers Work, with Animation, by ByteMonk (6 min)
hld-scaling.videoSearch: Load balancing and horizontal scaling explained

hld-caching.title: Caching and CDNs
hld-caching.summary: Keep a copy of expensive results close to where they are needed. Where the cache sits, how it is filled, what gets evicted and how stale data is handled are the four decisions in every caching design.

headings.text: Intuition: caches exist at every layer
Decision 1: how the cache is read and written
Decision 2: what to evict when memory is full

hld-caching.videoTitle: Cache Systems Every Developer Should Know, by ByteByteGo (6 min)

hld-data.title: Replication, sharding, CAP, consistency
hld-data.summary: The stateless tier scales by adding servers. Data does not. Replication copies it for availability and reads, partitioning splits it for size and writes, and the CAP theorem says what you give up when the network fails.
hld-data.videoTitle: CAP Theorem Simplified, by ByteByteGo (6 min)

hld-messaging.title: Queues, streams, event-driven systems
hld-messaging.summary: A queue lets one service hand work to another without waiting for it. That decoupling absorbs spikes and survives failures, and it introduces three questions you must answer every time. Can a message be lost, duplicated, or arrive out of order?
hld-messaging.videoTitle: Pub/Sub vs Message Queue vs Event Streaming (Kafka), by Coding With Taimoor (7 min)

hld-case-studies.title: Case studies: URL shortener, chat, feed
hld-case-studies.summary: Three classic designs worked end to end with the seven-step framework. A URL shortener, a chat system and a news feed. Each exercises a different hard part.
hld-case-studies.videoTitle: System Design Interview Question: Design URL Shortener, by Hayk Simonyan (13 min)
hld-case-studies.videoSearch: Case studies: URL shortener, chat, feed explained

lld-uml.title: UML: class, sequence, use case, state diagrams
lld-uml.summary: UML is the shared notation for explaining a design on a whiteboard. Four diagrams cover almost every interview. Class, sequence, use case and state. The part people get wrong is the six relationships between classes.
lld-uml.videoTitle: UML class diagrams, by Lucid Software (12 min)
lld-uml.videoSearch: UML: class, sequence, use case, state diagrams explained

lld-creational.title: Creational patterns
lld-creational.summary: Creational patterns answer one question. Who decides which object gets built, and how? Singleton, Factory Method, Abstract Factory, Builder and Prototype each remove a different kind of new from the code that should not care.
lld-creational.videoTitle: The Builder Pattern Explained and Implemented, by Geekific (8 min)

lld-structural.title: Structural patterns
lld-structural.summary: Structural patterns are about fitting objects together. Adapter converts an interface, Decorator adds behaviour, Proxy controls access, Facade simplifies, Composite treats a tree like a single object. Four of the five are wrappers that differ only in intent.
lld-structural.videoTitle: Structural Design Patterns: Adapter, Facade, Decorator, Proxy and others, by Hungry Back Dev (4 min)

lld-behavioral.title: Behavioral patterns
lld-behavioral.summary: Behavioural patterns decide who does what, and who tells whom. Strategy swaps an algorithm, Observer broadcasts a change, State changes behaviour with a lifecycle, Command turns a request into an object, Chain of Responsibility passes a request along a line.
lld-behavioral.videoTitle: The Observer Pattern Explained and Implemented, by Geekific (7 min)

lld-case-studies.title: Case studies: parking lot, rate limiter, splitwise
lld-case-studies.summary: The low-level design round, worked three times. A parking lot, a rate limiter and an expense splitter, each built with the same six steps and each showing where a pattern earns its place.

headings.text: The six steps for any LLD question

lld-case-studies.videoTitle: Parking Lot Design: LLD with Full Code Implementation, by Genie Ashwani (16 min)
lld-case-studies.videoSearch: Case studies: parking lot, rate limiter, splitwise explained

cn-url-journey.title: What happens when you open a URL

dbms-er-relational.title: ER model and the relational model

collab-editor.title: Real-time collaborative editor
collab-editor.tagline: Several people edit one document at once, with live cursors and no lost edits.

online-judge.title: Online judge
online-judge.tagline: Submit code, run it in a sandbox against hidden tests, get a verdict in seconds.

ecommerce.title: E-commerce with payments
ecommerce.tagline: Catalog, cart, orders and payments where money and stock never go out of sync.
